title: multipart: stabilize streaming + enforce file payload limits and content-type validation (OpenAI compat)
author: Anita Shah
description: Summary: Add robust multipart/form-data handling for file inputs on the API surface, enforce per-file and total payload limits, validate content-types for tool/function-calling file args, and stabilize streaming behavior for multipart uploads. Also bring the OpenAI-compat layer into parity for file upload semantics and error codes. Motivation: customers using file uploads for tool/function calling were seeing intermittent request aborts during streaming multipart uploads and inconsistent validation behavior between the Redwood API and the OpenAI-compat endpoints. This caused downstream tool runners to receive partial files or fail with unclear errors. This PR addresses three related gaps: 1) streaming/backpressure handling for multipart requests to ensure uploads are reliably forwarded to the runtime without truncation; 2) deterministic content-type validation and size limits (per-file and aggregate) to prevent resource-exhaustion attacks and provide clear user errors; 3) parity in OpenAI-compat endpoints so clients using standard OpenAI SDKs observe expected behavior and error semantics. Changes (high level): - Implement a streaming-aware multipart handler at the API gateway that preserves request boundaries while applying backpressure to the ingress buffers. The handler uses chunk-level checks and defers full buffering unless the part is small or explicitly required by downstream components. - Add configurable per-file size limit (default 25MB for hosted API) and aggregate upload cap (default 100MB); limits are enforced early with clear OpenAI-compatible error codes (413 / 400 with 'file_too_large' style JSON response). Limits are configurable per-deployment tier and can be overridden for Dedicated/Private in runtime config. - Content-type validation: require file part Content-Type header for tool/function-calling parameters; accept a allowlist and perform optional magic-bytes sniffing for common types (.json, .csv, image/*, application/pdf). - Update OpenAI-compat file endpoints to mirror Redwood API semantics and error messages. - Stabilize streaming: fix a race in the stream multiplexer that could drop the final chunk on fast uploads; improve tests that simulate slow clients and abrupt disconnects. - SDK compatibility: Python and TypeScript SDKs updated to expose new file-size errors and to use proper multipart boundaries when streaming. - Tests: extensive integration tests added simulating slow producers, large-file rejection, content-type mismatches, and OpenAI-compat client behavior. Rollout & migration notes: - Default limits are conservative and documented. Dedicated/Private customers can configure via the deployment config. - Added a compatibility flag control to enable the new strict content-type validation; enabled by default for hosted API. Follow-ups: - Telemetry to track top file content-types and rejected upload counts (ENG-4187). - Add per-customer policy to allow additional MIME types via Console UI (PM follow-up).

review_comments: Kai Morgan (review): The multipart streaming handler looks good overall. Two asks: 1) can we avoid copying parts into memory when the downstream supports streaming? 2) please add a unit test that simulates a mid-part client disconnect and verify the runtime doesn't receive a partial file.

Anita Shah (author): Addressed both: handler uses io.Pipe to stream parts when downstream declares streaming support, and added test 'test_client_disconnect_does_not_send_partial' in integration suite.

Riley Chen (review): We need clearer errors for content-type mismatch - return a 400 with a JSON body matching OpenAI compat (error.code = 'invalid_file_type'). Also add the allowlist to defaults.yaml.
Anita Shah (author): Updated error mapping and defaults.yaml. Added docs section noting which types are allowed by default and how to override per-deployment.
Luis Perez (approval): Verified behavior on dedicated staging with 50MB file acceptance override. Performance looks stable. Approving +1.
ci_notes: Initial CI run failed on linting and one flaky integration test (test_large_file_rejection) due to a race in the test harness; fixed in e5a9d0a, CI green on second run.
release_notes: Adds streaming-aware multipart/form-data support for file inputs; enforces configurable per-file and aggregate upload limits with OpenAI-compatible error codes; validates file Content-Type for tool/function-calling parameters; OpenAI-compat endpoints updated to match Redwood API behavior.
